experiments.title: Rule-world opener vs tier-skit opener
experiments.hypothesis: With the same footage and payoff, a rule-world opener ('In my world, everyone gets one slug for life', labelled fiction) holds viewers differently from a noob/pro/expert tier-skit opener. Untested hybrid: rule-world and gameplay proof never co-occurred in the pilot sample.
experiments.one_change: The opener only (first 2-3 s): rule card vs tier-skit framing. Footage, duel and payoff identical.
experiments.stop_rule: Read once at 48 h after each upload; no early peeking decisions.
experiments.threshold: To be set with ChatGPT before posting (research skills v1.1: predefined metric, window, stop rule and threshold).
experiments.design: One language at a time, on our own channel. Same footage and payoff, two openers. Block by language; randomise posting order.
experiments.limitations: Pilot evidence is exploratory (single AI coder, n=20). Prerequisite: film a real two-player Cinder Rift 1v1 round. Floppy never transforms and has no abilities; 'underdog' is framing, not a game rule.
experiments.next_action: Capture a real 1v1 round, then produce both 15 s versions (EN first).

variants.label: Tier-skit opener
variants.description: Same duel framed as an original noob/pro/expert tier skit (status reversal, no rule).

variants.label: Rule-world opener
variants.description: Rule card 'In my world, everyone gets one slug for life' (SKIT preset, fiction label), held-back reveal, Floppy underdog duel with real gameplay.
